feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no result for it. The candidate is the iteration 6 design (best raced so far, 255.7) with one change: sensor_positions y moved from 0.03 to 0.01 m for all seven sensors. Everything else is unchanged: x at +/-0.06 m, inner weights [-1, -0.75, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1], base_speed 1.3, kp 5.0, ki 0.02, kd 0.8, last_direction. Iteration 6 is the reference, so this race isolates the row move. The candidate is valid: every y is within the -0.06 to 0.08 m limit, and the weights are antisymmetric and within +/-2. Iterations 1 to 6 all held max_error at 0.053 to 0.064 m whatever the speed or gain (iterations 1 to 3, 5 and 6), which points to a geometry or lag cause rather than steering gain. Iteration 4 showed that the weights, not the wider x spread, cost finishes, so this candidate keeps the weights that gave iteration 5 and 6 their line-loss result of 0. Approval is for telemetry and a clean test of the lag hypothesis, not a performance claim.

What to change after the race, depending on what it shows:
- If line_loss stays at 0, oval finishes hold at 9 of 20 or more, and max_error falls below about 0.055 m on the s-bend and slalom, keep y at 0.01 m and move on to small tuning of kd or base_speed.
- If finishes drop to 0 while line_loss stays at 0, revert y to 0.03 m (iteration 6 as raced) and test base_speed 1.2 alone, since the row move hurt finishes.
- If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4 while max_error is below 0.05 m, lower kd from 0.8 to about 0.5 with y at 0.01 m, since a row closer to the axle changes the sensor-to-line reading more abruptly on bends.
requested_changes: Keep the iteration 6 design and change only sensor_positions y from 0.03 to 0.01 m for all seven sensors. Evidence: max_error has stayed at 0.053 to 0.064 m across iterations 1 to 6 whatever the speed or gain, and sensors at y = 0.03 m sit 3 cm ahead of the axle, so lag is a plausible cause.

If the race shows line_loss at 0 and max_error below about 0.055 m with finishes at 9 of 20 or more: keep y at 0.01 m and next test kd 0.5 only if steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.4. Evidence: iteration 6 oscillation was 0.32 on the oval and iteration 0 with kd 0.3 gave 0.07 to 0.16.

If finishes fall to 0 with line_loss still 0: revert y to 0.03 m and test base_speed 1.2 alone. Evidence: iteration 4 showed finishes can be lost when sensor geometry changes, and iteration 2 showed speed cuts alone did not fix drift, so this is a check on the speed side only.
